quote: And I see here, do you already have solar on your home?
stewart_read: This customer already owns solar and wants to add panels/battery — the schema's orphaned_flow trigger applies. The rep recognized it and adapted ("were you wanting to add panels or a battery") but never ran the full orphaned_flow checklist.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to recognize this as a formal branch, not an improvisation — the orphaned_flow section has specific required questions (system ownership/lease, original company, panel wattage, system working status) that should be run as a set once existing solar is disclosed.

quote: K. And then who are your panels with currently? What company did you buy them from?
stewart_read: Rep asks the original-company question from orphaned_flow correctly, and also captures ownership status ("do you own your system, or do you still make payments?" at 02:02). This is partial orphaned_flow coverage — two of four items captured.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the rep got two of the four orphaned_flow items right without a checklist prompting them — reinforce this as the right instinct, then close the gap on the two missed items.

quote: And then do you own your system, or do you still make payments?
stewart_read: The rep never asked whether the existing system is working (a hard_dq trigger per orphaned_flow: "We cannot service the existing system right now") or captured panel wattage. Both are required orphaned_flow items and neither was raised.
alternative_hypothesis: It is possible the rep judged this unnecessary since the customer is adding panels/battery rather than replacing the system, but the schema does not carve out that exception — the DQ check applies regardless of stated intent.
coaching_implication: Flag this as a coverage gap specific to orphaned leads: the rep needs the full four-question orphaned_flow set on file before the specialist visit, including system-working status, or risks booking an appointment for a system Ion cannot service.

quote: And then on Google Maps, it shows you have a pretty large tree in your backyard. Is that tree removed?
stewart_read: Customer's reply reveals the existing panel placement is suboptimal due to shading — a flat technical fact stated by the customer, not an enthusiasm signal. There is no schema-documented cross-sell or coaching pathway tied to tree removal for this call type.
coaching_implication: No specific coaching action indicated here beyond noting the rep captured the shading detail for the design team, which is the correct minimal action.

quote: Last time I checked, it was 849.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strong credit score confidently and specifically, more detail than the yes/no question required. Rep acknowledges it ("Oh, nice. Okay. So you're more than qualified then.") but this is a minor rapport moment, not a missed strategic play tied to any specific schema mechanism.
coaching_implication: No major coaching action needed — rep's acknowledgment was adequate and proportionate to the moment.

quote: Great. And then I have down here that you're paying about 200 a month on that electric bill. Is that accurate?
stewart_read: Rep surfaces a pre-loaded bill figure but the customer immediately softens it ("That sounds a little high") and then explains he can only estimate while driving. The rep accepts the vague answer and moves straight to bill-document collection without ever anchoring the number emotionally or re-confirming a firmer figure.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer is driving and admits he can't give a precise number, pushing harder in the moment could have been counterproductive — deferring the exact figure to the bill document itself is a reasonable adaptation.
coaching_implication: The rep should have flipped even the soft ballpark into forward motion — e.g., acknowledging the pain of a $200+ bill before pivoting to the document ask — rather than moving straight to logistics with no emotional bridge.

quote: Well, everything looks good here on my end. So the only thing I'll need from you, Ken, is just a copy of your kilowatt usage.
stewart_read: The rep pivots directly from an unconfirmed bill estimate to a logistics ask (bill document) without ever flipping the $200/month figure into a reason to act now — no alignment-against-utility framing, no curiosity hook about what the design might show.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be strategically deferring the emotional flip to the specialist call, consistent with setter_scope_discipline — the setter's job is to gather info, not sell. This is plausible, but the schema still expects at least a light anchor-and-flip before moving to logistics.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to insert one line connecting the bill pain to the appointment's value before pivoting to document collection — even a soft version like acknowledging the bill as the reason the specialist visit matters.

quote: Okay. Yeah. No problem. We can pick it up in a couple hours then. You have a wonderful rest of your day.
stewart_read: The call ends with no locked callback time, no specific hour block, no confirmed contact method, and no handshake question. "A couple hours" is not a rep-owned commitment.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer's driving situation genuinely prevented locking a time in this specific call, so this could be read as circumstance-driven rather than a rep skill gap.
coaching_implication: Even under a driving constraint, the rep should have proposed a specific callback window ("Can I call you back at 5 today?") rather than accepting the open-ended "couple hours" — this is a repeatable fix regardless of circumstance.
